paragraphs.text: 1. O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty.
paragraphs.original: प्र ससाहिषे पुरुहूत शत्रूञ्ज्येष्ठस्ते शुष्म इह रातिरस्तु ।
paragraphs.translit: pra sasāhiṣe puruhūta śatrūñjyeṣṭhaste śuṣma iha rātirastu |

paragraphs.text: In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches.
paragraphs.original: इन्द्रा भर दक्षिणेना वसूनि पतिः सिन्धूनामसि रेवतीनाम्
paragraphs.translit: indrā bhara dakṣiṇenā vasūni patiḥ sindhūnāmasi revatīnām

paragraphs.text: 2. Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance.
paragraphs.original: मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः परावत आ जगन्था परस्याः ।
paragraphs.translit: mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ parāvata ā jaganthā parasyāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Whetting thy bold and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us.
paragraphs.original: सृकं संशाय पविमिन्द्र तिग्मं वि शत्रून्ताळ्हि वि मृधो नुदस्व
paragraphs.translit: sṛkaṃ saṃśāya pavimindra tigmaṃ vi śatrūntāḷhi vi mṛdho nudasva

paragraphs.text: 3. Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o'er the people.
Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.
